content_text: "Go where there's dumb competition" is one of the better Mungerisms, but harder to put in practice than it sounds...few points of nuance 1. if you were to look for the dumbest competition, logic would say, look for a 'know-nothing' neophyte slash retail/casual investor, and then take the other side of their trade right off the bat, that means you're on the short side, which puts you at a severe disadvantage just bc of the "in practice" considerations (position sizing, risk/reward, max payoff vs max loss) you can try and invert this, but there really are no "dumb" short sellers...they're forced into higher levels of homework to offset the practical disadvantages above 2. a lot of times, the 'know-nothing' investor, they are chasing what are basically levered equity stubs or OTM call options the expected value will be negative, say a 0.1% chance of 10x'ing vs. 99.9% chance it goes to zero. but in practice, u can't take that risk, something like gamestop or a fartcoin can nuke ur account and end ur career. that's why "go where there's dumb competition" doesn't really work 3. the best inversion of this, in practice, would be "don't go where there's smart competition." today, that usually translates to: "am I going up against BAM/MLP/P72 etc in this trade idea?" simplest definition of that, would be..."am I playing for a discrete/binary catalyst on a sub-3 month time horizon?" because that's their game...u have literally sought out the toughest possible competition. worth applying as a filter for any/all ideas u see, on here or otherwise, bc u will recognize - "wow u could not have picked a worse poker table to sit at." (END) overall, Munger references this principle in a separate question: Q: If you were starting out with a small amount of capital, where would you focus? A: I wouldn’t go where the big boys have to be, trying to decide whether Merck’s pipeline is better than Pfizer’s. I’d go where there are market inefficiencies and your work could lead to knowing important things that other people didn’t. thats abt as much as u can hope for in "go where there's dumb competition"... "don't go where the big boys are."
